wines.name: Les Parcelles XX, Grand Cru Bouzy

peak.note: Built on structured Pinot Noir from a warm, ripe year with the house's characteristic vinous depth and low dosage, this Champagne is still tightly wound and fresh, with red fruit and chalky minerality only beginning to gain the brioche and toasted nuances that further cellaring will bring.

The 2013 vintage's firm acidity and tight chalky structure are now softening into layers of brioche, toasted hazelnut and baked apple, while Charles Heidsieck's long cellar ageing on lees gives the mousse a creamy polish that still has plenty of energy to carry it forward.

This prestige blanc de blancs is moving from its youthful citrus and chalky tension into a more complex phase of toasted brioche, hazelnut and honeyed richness, with the long cellar aging on lees giving it fine mousse and the structure to keep evolving gracefully.

Zero-dosage Cava built on Xarel·lo's firm acidity and saline backbone is showing fresh orchard fruit and a creamy, gently toasty mousse as its lees ageing integrates, but with no sugar to cushion it the wine will lose vibrancy and turn austere if kept too long.

The 2020 harvest delivered ripe, beautifully balanced Chardonnay in Kent, and this blanc de blancs still shows tightly wound citrus and green apple energy with chalky minerality, while extended lees ageing is only beginning to add brioche and toasted almond richness that will deepen with time in bottle.

The 2020 harvest in Kent delivered ripe, healthy fruit with well-balanced acidity, so this rosé is showing vibrant red berry and citrus freshness that is just beginning to gain gentle brioche and toasty complexity from its time on lees, with the high acidity giving it a long and graceful runway ahead.

This youthful Sicilian blend is at its freshest right now, with crisp citrus, white flower and almond notes from Catarratto and Inzolia that are best enjoyed young before the bright acidity and aromatic lift begin to fade.

This is a youthful, fresh-style Alvarinho and Trajadura blend built for early enjoyment, so right now it should show vivid citrus and stone fruit, bright acidity and a light spritz that will gradually fade as the primary fruit softens.

This young Picpoul is at its most vibrant right now, with piercing citrus, saline minerality and crisp acidity from the Mediterranean-influenced Pinet terroir, a freshness that is meant to be enjoyed in youth before the delicate aromatics begin to fade.

Still in its bright, saline youth, this Muscadet shows crisp citrus and green apple fruit wrapped in a subtle creamy texture from its time resting on the lees, and it will gradually gain a touch of waxy, stony complexity while keeping its refreshing mineral edge.

Still in its vibrant infancy, this Albariño shows crisp citrus, white peach and saline freshness driven by Atlantic acidity, and it is best enjoyed young before the aromatic lift softens into more honeyed, waxy tones.

This young Grillo is showing bright citrus, white blossom and saline freshness, and its stainless-steel-driven, unoaked style means it is best enjoyed in its vibrant youth before the aromatics begin to fade.

This youthful Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc is at its most vivid right now, with zesty citrus, passionfruit and fresh herbal lift that come from its screwcap seal and bright acidity, and these primary aromas will gradually soften toward more muted, savory notes with age.

As a very young Alte Reben Riesling from old ungrafted vines on Mosel slate, it is currently dominated by primary lime, green apple and stony mineral tension with racy acidity that needs time to integrate before honeyed petrol and layered complexity emerge.

This entry-level Alsace Riesling is still primary and tightly wound, with crisp citrus and green-apple fruit over a stony, mineral backbone, and its firm acidity will carry it gracefully as petrol and honeyed notes slowly emerge with bottle age.

Still youthful and tightly coiled, the wine shows crisp citrus, flinty minerality and fresh herbal lift that are gradually knitting together with a touch more texture and roundness as it settles from the generous, ripe-leaning growing season.

Still a young, tightly wound Garganega showing crisp citrus, almond and chalky mineral freshness, and its volcanic-soil acidity will gradually fold into a more rounded, honeyed texture with time in bottle.

Still a very young Cortese, this Lugarara bottling shows crisp citrus, green apple and a saline mineral edge from its Gavi di Gavi clay and limestone soils, and it will gain a touch of almond and honeyed texture with a little bottle age while keeping its fresh acidity.

This entry-level Langenlois Grüner is still in its fresh, primary phase, showing crisp citrus, green apple and its signature white pepper snap that comes from the region's cool nights and loess soils, and it should gain only modest softness and a touch of honeyed texture rather than real complexity, so it is best enjoyed young.
This young Chablis is still tightly wound, with crisp citrus, green apple and a flinty mineral edge that should gradually soften into honeyed, savory complexity as the bottle rests in a cool cellar.

This young Viognier is in its fresh, aromatic first phase, with apricot, white peach and floral notes that are best enjoyed while the fruit stays vibrant, as the wine is built for early drinking rather than long cellaring.

This Godello from Bierzo's slate and granite soils is still in its vibrant youth, with fresh citrus, orchard fruit and a saline mineral edge that should gradually gain texture and honeyed nuance as it settles in bottle.

This entry-level Vermentino is built for youthful freshness, so its bright citrus, green apple and saline Mediterranean character are at their most vibrant now, and it will gradually lose aromatic lift and zest rather than gain complexity with cellaring.

This young Viura is still in its fresh, primary phase, showing crisp citrus and orchard fruit with a saline, herbal edge, and its natural acidity and fine lees contact should let it gain subtle nutty texture with a little bottle time.

This Grenache Gris is still in its fresh, youthful phase, showing ripe orchard fruit, a waxy herbal edge and gentle saline minerality, and its modest acidity and lack of oak mean it is best enjoyed while the aromatics remain vibrant rather than being cellared for long.

This is a fresh, unoxidized Bordeaux Blanc whose citrus and green-herb Sauvignon Blanc brightness is currently well supported by the Sémillon's waxy texture, and because it is a modest entry-level cuvée made for early enjoyment it will gradually lose its aromatic vibrancy rather than gain complexity with long cellaring.

Still youthful and tightly wound, the old-vine Swartland fruit is showing crisp orchard and citrus notes with a saline, stony backbone that should slowly broaden into honeyed, waxy complexity as the wine settles in bottle.

This youthful Mâcon-Villages Chardonnay is in its fresh, fruit-driven phase right now, showing crisp orchard and citrus notes with gentle minerality, and since it was made without oak ageing or heavy concentration it is best enjoyed young before the vibrant fruit begins to fade.

This unoaked Beaujolais Chardonnay from granitic and limestone soils is showing fresh orchard fruit, citrus and a stony mineral edge, and while the warm, generous 2023 season gave it ripe texture and good body, its modest structure favours enjoying it young rather than waiting for real evolution.

The generous, ripe 2023 fruit gives this Aligoté more roundness than the variety usually shows, yet its bright citrus and saline tension remain intact, so it is drinking vividly now and should gain gentle honeyed, nutty complexity in the near term before the zesty freshness begins to soften.

Still youthful and fresh, with bright orchard fruit and gentle oak that are beginning to knit together, though the wine is unlikely to gain much complexity beyond its medium-term window given the typical California Chardonnay structure and moderate acidity.

This generous, ripe-leaning 2023 Marsannay Blanc is showing open, fleshy orchard fruit with a gentle chalky tension, and while approachable now, a little more bottle time should knit the oak and acidity together into a more savory, layered wine.

Still primary and tightly wound, this cool-sited Chardonnay shows citrus, flinty reductive reflexes and taut acidity that will gradually give way to creamier, nuttier complexity as the oak integrates.

This generous, ripe-leaning 2023 Vau de Vey is still tightly coiled with citrus, white flower and crushed-shell minerality, and the vintage's ample fruit and moderate acidity mean it will broaden into a more textured, honeyed-saline profile with a few years of bottle age.

Still tightly wound and youthful, this cool-climate Chardonnay shows bright citrus, flinty reduction and crisp acidity that should gradually integrate with its oak and settle into a more layered, mineral-driven profile as it ages.

This Aligoté from Vosne-Romanée's Cathiard is showing its youthful citrus and green apple vibrancy while the warm, ripe 2022 vintage lends a rounder, more textured mid-palate that softens the grape's typical sharp acidity, so it drinks generously now and will gain subtle honeyed and stony complexity over the coming years.

This Saint-Romain from a warm, generous white Burgundy vintage is showing ripe orchard fruit and a touch of oak spice, with the high-altitude, limestone-driven acidity of the appellation keeping it fresh while the texture slowly integrates and gains a hazelnut and honeyed complexity.

wines.producer: Domaine du Château Philippe le Hardi
wines.name: Saint-Aubin, En Vesveau

peak.note: This generous, sun-ripened Saint-Aubin from a warm, early-harvest vintage is showing ripe orchard fruit and gentle hazelnut notes, with a firm limestone-driven mineral backbone that is only now starting to integrate with its rounder texture and subtle oak.

This generous, ripe 2023 white Burgundy from a village-level Chassagne premier cru is still in its tight, youthful phase, with fresh orchard fruit and a chalky mineral edge that will gain nutty, savory depth as the generous vintage fruit settles into the wine.

Still youthful and tightly wound, this Puligny from a generous, ripe vintage shows fresh citrus, white flowers and subtle oak, with the ripe fruit and bright acidity promising mineral depth and honeyed complexity as it settles into bottle.

Still tightly wound and primary, this generous yet well-balanced 2023 Les Blanchots is showing ripe citrus and orchard fruit over a firm mineral spine, and it needs time in the cellar for its oyster-shell salinity and richer, honeyed complexity to emerge.

This village-level Meursault from a warm, generous vintage is still youthful and tightly knit, with ripe orchard fruit and gentle toasty oak that are just beginning to integrate, while bright acidity and a limestone-driven mineral core promise a more complex, nutty, honeyed profile as it settles in bottle.

This is a young, unoaked southern Rhône rosé built on Grenache and Cinsault, so it is at its most vibrant now with crisp red berry, citrus zest and a saline, herbal edge that will gradually soften and lose freshness with time in bottle.

This Grenache and Cinsault rosé is at its freshest right now, with crisp red berry fruit, delicate floral lift and a bright, dry finish that will gradually soften and lose vibrancy as it ages, so it is best enjoyed young and chilled.

As a young Provence rosé built on Grenache and Cinsault, it is at its freshest right now, with crisp red-berry fruit, a saline mineral edge and lively acidity that will gently soften into rounder, softer fruit over the coming year rather than gain complexity.

This pale, dry Provence rosé is built for freshness rather than longevity, so it shows its best now with vivid red berry, citrus zest and a saline, herbal lift that will gradually soften and lose its crispness with extended bottle age.

As a fresh, unoaked Negroamaro rosé built on bright red berry and citrus-peel fruit with a saline finish, it is now past its most vibrant stage and is gradually losing aromatic lift, so it should be enjoyed well chilled and soon.

This is a pale, dry Provence rosé built for freshness rather than age, so its crisp red berry fruit, citrus zest and saline lift are at their most vivid now, and the bright acidity from the cooler, balanced growing season will begin to soften into dull, muted fruit the longer it sits in the cellar.

This pale, dry Provence rosé is at its most vibrant while young, with crisp citrus, white peach and delicate red berry fruit lifted by saline freshness, and it will gradually lose its aromatic sparkle and soften into a rounder, less lively style with bottle age.

This Mourvèdre-led Bandol rosé is still in its fresh, taut youth, with crisp red-berry fruit, saline minerality and herbal garrigue notes that are best enjoyed before the vivid fruit begins to soften into a more savory, evolved character.

This is an approachable, entry-level Nero d'Avola whose bright dark-cherry fruit and soft tannins are showing best while still youthful, and since the 2023 Sicilian harvest was marked by a cool, wet spring followed by drought-stressed summer heat, the wine offers moderate concentration that favors enjoying it fresh rather than cellaring for long.

This young Languedoc Syrah is currently showing exuberant dark fruit and peppery spice with fairly firm tannins, and a little bottle time should soften its structure and bring out savory, garrigue-tinged complexity.

Still youthful and fruit-driven, this Malbec shows ripe plum and blackberry with supple tannins from a balanced Mendoza growing season, and it should gain softness and subtle spice complexity with a little more bottle age.

This entry-level Montepulciano d'Abruzzo is still youthful and fruit-driven, showing vibrant dark cherry and plum with soft, supple tannins that make it best enjoyed fresh rather than cellared for long.

Still a youthful, fruit-driven Carignan with vibrant red and dark berry character and lively acidity, best enjoyed fresh and slightly cool while the rustic tannins remain supple and approachable rather than needing extended cellaring.

This warm-vintage Grenache-Syrah blend is showing generous ripe dark fruit and soft, rounded tannins in its youth, and while it will gain a little savory, peppery complexity with short cellaring, its easy-drinking southern Rhône structure favors enjoying it fresh over long aging.

Still youthful and vibrant, the bright red berry fruit and supple tannins of this old-vine McLaren Vale Grenache are showing generous charm now, while the fine structure suggests it will gain savoury, spicy complexity with careful cellaring.

The Tempranillo is settling into a harmonious phase where the oak influence from its barrel ageing has integrated with the ripe red cherry and dried herb fruit, giving supple tannins and savoury, leathery complexity that makes it very approachable now.

Fashioned from biodynamically farmed old-vine Grenache and Syrah in a warm, dry year, it is showing ripe dark fruit, garrigue and peppery spice with supple tannins that make it appealing now, while its freshness suggests it will gain complexity with a few more years in the cellar.

The 2024 Rhône vintage was cooler and more irregular than recent years, so this young Lirac shows bright red and dark fruit with fresh acidity and supple tannins, and it will gain spice and softness with a little time in bottle.

Frog's Leap's restrained, lower-alcohol Zinfandel style keeps the bright red cherry and raspberry fruit fresh while the peppery spice and soft tannins gradually integrate, so it is drinking vibrantly now and should gain subtle earthy complexity before the fruit begins to fade.

Still tightly wound and primary, the dark-fruited Grenache core and peppery Syrah structure are wrapped in youthful tannins that need time to knit together, so patient cellaring will reward you with greater garrigue, leather and spice complexity as the warm, concentrated vintage fruit settles.

Still youthful and tightly wound, with bright acidity and red cherry and dried herb fruit just beginning to pick up the leather, tobacco and dill-tinged spice that long cask ageing and the house's traditional approach will deepen, so it rewards patience or a long decant.

This Merlot and Cabernet Franc blend from a ripe, generous Right Bank vintage is still in its youthful fruit-driven phase, with plush dark plum and black cherry flavors, supple tannins and fresh acidity, and it will gain complexity and savory depth with further cellaring.

This sun-ripened Saint-Estèphe is still in its primary phase, with dense dark fruit and firm but ripe tannins that are slowly softening, so it rewards decanting now while the structure continues to integrate for the long term.

This approachable, fruit-forward Cabernet from a generous cool-leaning California vintage is showing ripe dark berry and soft tannins now, and its moderate structure means it will gently soften and gain subtle savory complexity over a few years rather than improve dramatically.

The 2019 Merlot-driven blend from this right-bank satellite appellation is still showing youthful plush dark plum and blackberry fruit with ripe, polished tannins from the warm, dry growing season, and it is just starting to layer in cedar and truffle notes that will deepen as the Cabernet Franc adds lift and structure.

The 2016 Pauillac vintage gave structured, fresh wines with firm tannins and vivid cassis fruit, so this bottling is still in its youthful, tightly knit phase and benefits from decanting or further cellaring as the tannins soften and cedar and graphite notes emerge.

The 2010 vintage's firm tannic structure and bright acidity have now softened into a polished frame, with dark fruit giving way to graphite, cigar box and gravelly earth that are typical of Pessac-Léognan, though the wine still has the backbone to hold and evolve gracefully.

As the second wine of a leading Pessac-Léognan estate from a ripe, structured vintage, it is beginning to soften and show dark fruit, graphite and smoky cedar, though its firm tannins still reward a little decanting or further patience.

This second wine of Léoville Barton is still youthful, with dense cassis and graphite fruit framed by firm but ripening tannins, so decanting now rewards patience while the sun-drenched 2018 concentration slowly softens into cedar and tobacco complexity.

As the second wine of Rauzan-Ségla, Ségla from this cool-fruited, structured Margaux vintage is shedding its youthful grip and now shows perfumed violet and cassis notes with fine-grained tannins, though it still rewards a little decanting before it fully relaxes.

As the second wine of Léoville-Poyferré, it shows ripe dark cassis and plum fruit with polished tannins and fresh acidity from the warm, concentrated 2019 harvest, so it is already approachable with a short decant yet still tightly knit and gaining savory, cedary complexity.

The wine is still in a tightly coiled, youthful phase where dense cassis and dark plum fruit dominate, but early hints of cedar, graphite and savory earth are emerging as the firm, finely grained tannins slowly begin to soften, so decanting well ahead of service is rewarded.

Still youthful and primary, with ripe dark berry and wild herb fruit framed by firm, slightly rustic Monastrell tannins that need a little more time to soften, though it already shows a fresh, sun-ripened character from Alicante's warm, dry growing season.

As a young Sangiovese-based Chianti it is currently showing vibrant cherry and red plum fruit with lively acidity and fine-grained tannins that will soften and gain savory, earthy complexity with a little time in the cellar.

The 2020 Douro vintage delivered ripe, concentrated fruit with firm yet polished tannins, so this blend of Touriga Nacional, Touriga Franca and Tinta Roriz is still tightly knit and primary, with dark berry fruit, violet and mineral spice that will gradually soften and gain savoury complexity with further bottle age.

Azelia's single-vineyard Dolcetto from the Bricco dell'Oriolo cru is moving out of its primary exuberance into a more savory, integrated phase, with the plush black cherry and licorice fruit from a warm, ripe vintage now framed by softening tannins and its signature almond-bitter finish.

Bright, juicy and floral with crunchy red and dark berry fruit and a graphite-tinged mineral edge, this slate-grown Mencía from a warm, ripe vintage is already approachable thanks to its supple tannins, yet it has the acidity and structure to gain savory, earthy complexity over the next several years.

This light-bodied, fresh Cinsault is showing bright red cherry, strawberry and floral notes with soft tannins, and its low structure means it is best enjoyed young and slightly chilled while the vibrant fruit remains at the forefront.

Still youthful and fruit-driven, with fresh cherry and a touch of dried-fruit richness from the Amarone pomace refermentation, and the supple tannins and bright acidity are gradually integrating to add savory depth.

This is Vajra's fresh, entry-level Langhe Nebbiolo, so right now it shows bright red cherry, rose petal and a light spicy lift with supple tannins that suit youthful drinking, and it will gain some savory complexity but never the structure for long cellaring.

Still youthful and tightly wound, the cool-sited Firs Syrah shows dark berry fruit, black pepper and savoury, peppery spice held in check by fine, fresh acidity and firm but ripe tannins that need time to soften and let the more complex layers emerge.

Coming from a hot, drought-stressed growing season, this Rosso shows ripe red cherry and warm spice with softer acidity than cooler years, so it is already approachable and charming while its fine-grained tannins keep it fresh enough to hold a few more years in the cellar.

Coming from a hot, dry growing season that gave concentrated fruit with ripe tannins, the wine is still youthful and primary, showing dark plum and black cherry fruit with firm but polished structure that should soften and gain savory, spicy complexity with further bottle age.

Born of a hot, drought-stressed growing season, this Brunello shows ripe dark cherry and warm spice with firm but polished tannins that are only just beginning to soften, so it is approachable now yet will gain complexity and savory depth with further cellaring.

Rostaing's Ampodium, a Syrah with a small touch of Viognier-free purity from the Côte Brune, is still tightly wound and primary, with dark berry fruit, violet and peppery spice wrapped in fine-grained tannins that need a few more years in the cellar to unwind into the smoky, savory complexity this site is known for.

Coste di Rose from this warm but well-balanced vintage shows ripe red cherry, rose petal and sweet spice with fine, polished tannins that are still tightly wound, so it rewards patience or a long decant while the fruit slowly gains savory, tarry depth.

This young Chiroubles is still in its fresh, primary fruit phase, with bright red cherry and violet notes and a lightly crunchy structure that will gradually soften and gain savory depth, though the cool, variable growing season gave it a more delicate, lower-alcohol profile than the riper recent vintages, so it rewards early to mid-term enjoyment over long cellaring.

A regional-level Bourgogne from a cool, wet, challenging growing season, this wine is still in its primary youthful phase with bright red cherry and raspberry fruit and lively acidity that will soften gradually into more savory, earthy complexity with a little bottle age.

This cool-vintage Ingelheim Spätburgunder is moving from primary red-cherry fruit toward savory, earthy complexity, with its fresh acidity and fine-grained tannins giving it a graceful, medium-term trajectory rather than a long haul.

Still youthful and tightly wound, with bright red cherry and wild strawberry fruit sitting over fine-grained tannins and a savoury stem-spice edge that will soften and gain forest-floor complexity as the wine settles in bottle.

This regional Bourgogne Rouge from a warm, ripe vintage is showing generous red cherry and raspberry fruit with soft tannins and supple texture, making it charming and approachable now, though its modest structure means it is best enjoyed in its fresh youth rather than held for long evolution.

This cool-climate, whole-bunch-influenced Pinot Noir from the Hemel-en-Aarde area is still in its taut, primary youth, with bright red cherry and crunchy herbal spice, and its fine acidity and supple tannin structure will let it gain savory, earthy complexity with cellaring.

A frost-reduced, lightly cropped 2021 in the Côte Chalonnaise, this Givry is showing bright red cherry and wild strawberry fruit with a fresh, slightly rustic structure, and while it is already charming, a little more bottle time should soften its firm, mineral-edged tannins and bring out earthy, forest-floor complexity.

This Willamette Valley Pinot from the Eola-Amity Hills is moving out of its tight, youthful fruit phase into a more layered stage where red cherry and wild strawberry are gaining forest floor, dried herb and subtle spice, while the structure from a warm, well-ripened vintage keeps it fresh and gives it room to keep evolving.

Still youthful and primary, this cool-climate Sta. Rita Hills Pinot shows bright red cherry, wild herb and crushed stone with fine-grained tannins that are gradually integrating, and the wine should gain silkier texture and savory complexity as the fruit settles over the next few years.

This generous, ripe-fruited Chorey from a warm, abundant Burgundy vintage is currently showing plush red cherry and raspberry with soft tannins, so it is charming young but will gain savoury complexity and better focus with a little more bottle age.

This village-level Côte de Nuits Pinot Noir from a cool, frost-reduced but concentrated vintage is moving from primary red-cherry fruit into earthier, more savory territory with softened tannins, and it should drink best over the coming years before the fruit begins to fade.

This old-vine Gevrey-Chambertin from a warm, ripe vintage is still in its primary phase, showing dark cherry and plum fruit with supple tannins that are only just beginning to integrate, so it will reward patience as the earthy, spiced complexity of the village emerges.

Still youthful and tightly coiled, with dark cherry and wild herb fruit framed by fine-grained tannins and bright acidity that are gradually knitting together, so patience will reward with greater savoury complexity and silkier texture.

Still tightly wound and dominated by primary red cherry, crushed raspberry and a stony, mineral edge, the wine is showing the generous ripeness of a warm, plentiful vintage tempered by Les Sizies' fine-grained structure and the gentle whole-cluster spice typical of de Montille, so it rewards patience as the tannins knit and savory depth emerges.

Chevillon's old-vine Nuits-Saint-Georges is still tight and firmly structured in this cool, frost-reduced vintage, with bright red cherry and iron-tinged mineral tension that needs more bottle time to soften its tannins and unfold savory, earthy complexity.

This is still a tightly wound young wine whose bright red cherry fruit and fine-grained, silky tannins are only beginning to knit together, and the generous ripeness of the vintage promises a seductive, floral Volnay as the stony Carelle terroir slowly emerges with bottle age.

Saint Martin is Laroche's entry-level village Chablis, and this cool, wet, difficult vintage produced bright, lean wines with crisp acidity and modest concentration that are best enjoyed fresh for their citrus and oyster-shell tension rather than long cellaring.

This entry-level Southern Rhône blend is showing bright, juicy red and black fruit with soft tannins and a peppery Syrah lift, and because it is built for early charm rather than structure it is best enjoyed while that youthful fruit remains vibrant.

Côte du Py's volcanic schist soils give this Morgon a firm mineral backbone beneath its ripe black cherry and violet fruit, and the tannins are still tightly knit, so it is youthful and a little reserved now but should gain savory, game-tinged depth with further bottle age.

This Haut-Médoc cru bourgeois from a warm, generous but uneven Bordeaux vintage is still tight and primary, showing dark fruit and firm, youthful tannins that need time in the cellar to soften and integrate.

As the second wine of Doisy-Védrines, it is showing bright apricot, honey and citrus-zest fruit with lively acidity from a sunny, well-balanced botrytis harvest, and it is drinkable now for its charm but will gain complexity and richness with further cellaring.

This young Recioto is currently showing vibrant cherry, plum and violet fruit with a plush sweetness balanced by fresh acidity, and as the dried-grape concentration and soft tannins integrate it will gain deeper notes of chocolate, spice and dried fruit.

Still a coiled, primary wine, its honeyed apricot, quince and orange-peel fruit is held taut by the searing Furmint acidity that will keep it fresh, and it will slowly unfold into saffron, dried fruit and spice complexity with cellaring.

Having aged for years in small chestnut and oak caratelli before bottling, this Vin Santo is now showing integrated notes of dried apricot, roasted hazelnut, caramel and orange peel, with its high natural acidity keeping the luscious sweetness lively and the finish long.

Still primary and exuberant, this Vidal icewine shows bright apricot, honeyed pineapple and lychee fruit held in tension by its piercing natural acidity, which will carry it gracefully toward richer notes of marmalade, dried fruit and caramel as it ages.

Graham's LBV from the 2019 harvest is still youthful and fruit-driven, with dense blackberry, violet and dark chocolate character gradually softening as its tannins integrate, so it rewards decanting now but will gain extra polish and complexity with further bottle age.

w-corte-giara-recioto-della-valpolicella.hook: Valpolicella's sweet red, usually from Corvina, the grape this corner of Italy famously dries for Amarone.

w-corte-giara-recioto-della-valpolicella.taste: Sweet dark cherry and raisin, rich and smooth, with a little tartness so it doesn't feel sticky.
w-corte-giara-recioto-della-valpolicella.grape: Usually Corvina, with Rondinella: Corvina brings tart cherry fruit and only light-to-medium tannin, the drying feel red wine leaves on your gums, and it turns rich and raisin-like when the grapes are dried.
w-corte-giara-recioto-della-valpolicella.place: It's from Valpolicella in the Veneto, north-east Italy, where Lake Garda and the Adriatic soften the climate and where the local tradition of drying grapes for months concentrates sugar and flavour.

w-dobogo-tokaji-noble-late-harvest-mylit.hook: Tokaj's autumn mists encourage noble rot, a helpful mould that concentrates the grapes' sweetness.
w-dobogo-tokaji-noble-late-harvest-mylit.pitch: It's a sweet white from Tokaj in Hungary, tasting of honey and ripe pear and apple, with a lovely fresh zing. It's sweet without ever feeling heavy, so it's perfect with fruit puddings or blue cheese.
w-dobogo-tokaji-noble-late-harvest-mylit.taste: Honey and ripe orchard fruit like pear and apple, sweet but kept bright and lively by mouth-watering acidity.
w-dobogo-tokaji-noble-late-harvest-mylit.grape: Usually Furmint, Hungary's backbone grape, which gives high acidity, meaning that fresh, mouth-watering zing, plus orchard fruit and honey notes.
w-dobogo-tokaji-noble-late-harvest-mylit.place: Tokaj in Hungary has a continental climate (warm summers, cold winters), and its autumn mists encourage noble rot, a helpful mould that concentrates the grapes' sugar and flavour.

w-chateau-larose-perganson-chateau-laros.hook: From the Haut-Médoc, on Bordeaux's gravelly Left Bank, where blends usually lean on Cabernet Sauvignon.
w-chateau-larose-perganson-chateau-laros.pitch: This is a young, proper Bordeaux red, full of blackcurrant and cedar with a firm, drying grip. With a rich cut of beef that grip softens and the fruit opens up, so every mouthful of meat makes the wine taste better.
w-chateau-larose-perganson-chateau-laros.taste: Blackcurrant and cedar wood, full in the mouth, with fresh acidity (a mouth-watering zing) and firm tannin, the drying grip you feel on your gums.
w-chateau-larose-perganson-chateau-laros.grape: Cabernet Sauvignon, usually the lead grape here alongside Merlot, has thick skins that give deep colour, blackcurrant and cedar flavours and firm tannin.
w-chateau-larose-perganson-chateau-laros.place: The Haut-Médoc is on Bordeaux's Left Bank, with gravel soils and a mild, sea-influenced climate softened by the Gironde estuary, which is why the blends there usually lean on Cabernet Sauvignon for structure.

w-doisy-vedrines-chateau-petit-vedrines.grape: Sémillon, usually the main grape with some Sauvignon Blanc, brings honeyed flavour and a waxy texture, and it easily catches noble rot (botrytis), a helpful mould that shrivels the grapes and concentrates their sugar.
w-doisy-vedrines-chateau-petit-vedrines.place: Sauternes is the sweet-wine corner of Bordeaux, where the mild, damp climate near the Gironde estuary helps Sémillon make rich, sweet wines that can age for decades.

c-cubitt-elderflower-spritz.pitch: It's a light, bubbly gin spritz with floral elderflower, fresh lemon and a low-sugar tonic, so it's refreshing and only gently sweet. Perfect for anyone who wants something easy and summery to start with, especially gin lovers or anyone who usually orders a glass of Prosecco.
c-cubitt-elderflower-spritz.taste: Light, floral and fizzy, with zesty citrus from the gin and lemon and a soft sweetness from the elderflower.

explain.means: A long, bubbly drink topped up with sparkling wine or a fizzy mixer, so it tastes lighter and more refreshing than a short cocktail.
A gin from the Hayman's family distillers with a strong citrus character, which gives the drink a bright, zesty lift.
The flower of the elder bush, used to give drinks a sweet, floral, slightly grapey taste; here it brings the gentle sweetness.
A lighter tonic water with less sugar and fewer calories than a standard tonic, adding bubbles and a soft bitter edge without making the drink sweeter.

dishes.why: The lemony, bubbly spritz is like a squeeze of citrus with the salty oysters and keeps every mouthful fresh.

dishes.dish: Sea Bream Crudo, Preserved Lemon, Dill
dishes.why: Its light citrus and floral notes match the lemon and dill without drowning out the delicate raw fish.

alts.when: no alcohol, but still light and bubbly
no gin, or something fruitier and a little more bittersweet

Gin

Bubbles and a soft bitter edge, with less sugar than standard tonic

qs.q: What is the main difference between the Cubitt Elderflower Spritz and the Fruit Cup Spritz?
opts: The Cubitt Elderflower Spritz is built on gin with elderflower and tonic; the Fruit Cup Spritz is built on two vermouths and triple sec with soda water
The Cubitt Elderflower Spritz is non-alcoholic; the Fruit Cup Spritz is made with gin
The Cubitt Elderflower Spritz is built on vodka and olive brine; the Fruit Cup Spritz is built on gin

qs.why: Both are topped with Prosecco, but the Cubitt Elderflower Spritz is a floral gin drink while the Fruit Cup Spritz is a vermouth-and-orange drink.

c-fruit-cup-spritz.pitch: It's a light, bubbly spritz made with English white and red vermouths and an orange liqueur, so it's fruity, gently herby and a little bittersweet. Great for anyone who likes a Pimm's-style summer drink or an Italian-style aperitivo, which just means a light pre-dinner drink to wake up the appetite.
c-fruit-cup-spritz.taste: Fruity and fizzy, with soft orange, a gentle herby bittersweetness from the vermouths and a light, easy finish.
c-fruit-cup-spritz.spirit: vermouth (white and red), topped with Prosecco

explain.means: A wine flavoured with herbs, spices and botanicals and strengthened with a little spirit; the white one here is lighter and more floral, the red is richer and more bittersweet.
An English producer of vermouths and bitter liqueurs; this spritz uses two of their vermouths, an English White and an Estate Red.
A brand of triple sec, which is a sweet orange liqueur, giving the drink its orangey fruitiness.
A British name for long, fruity summer drinks like Pimm's, so it's a handy comparison for guests.

dishes.why: The fruity, bittersweet vermouths sit nicely with the sweet figs, bitter leaves and salty blue cheese.
A light, bittersweet spritz is a classic partner for salty cured meats and keeps your mouth refreshed between bites.

alts.when: they'd prefer gin, or something more floral and citrusy
something stronger and short, still with red vermouth
